## My data

  The Fairness dataset is the Adult dataset. Each row represents one person, and the data includes information regarding demographics and income. This dataset contains 5000 rows. The dataset came from the 1994 Census database. The Sports dataset contains racing results from the 2023 Boston Marathon. This dataset contains 26598 rows. Each row represents one person who participated in the race, and the data shows information such as age group, gender, finishing time, and placement.

WRITE (2–3 sentences):My prediction was that people with higher education levels would have higher income rates. The plot shows that prof-school has the highest income rate, followed by Doctors and Masters. Preschool has the lowest, and most of the 1st-12th grades are about the same level at less than 10%. Since each bar represents a proportion of its own group, education levels with different numbers of people can be compared fairly (except for the ones with low sample sizes, like preschool).

WRITE (2–3 sentences): The Doctorate group has the widest standard-error range, with an SE of 0.0584 and a sample size of 61. A wide range indicates greater uncertainty in the estimated income rate, especially for groups with smaller sample sizes. The plot keeps smaller groups visible by displaying every education group, including those with very few observations, rather than excluding them.

WRITE (2 sentences): The plot shows the proportion of participants in each age group who finished in the top 100 overall. Shares rather than counts allow age groups of different sizes to be compared fairly.

### B2 · A mean with its two spreads

```{r}
#| label: fig-b2
#| ref.label: b2
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Mean in each group, with ± one standard error and group size."
#| fig-alt: "  The plot compares mean finishing times across age groups with standard-error ranges and sample sizes."
```

```{r}
#| label: b2-check
#| include: false
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-b2
#| tbl-cap: "Group size, mean, sd and se."
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(b2_summary, digits = 3)
```

WRITE (2–3 sentences): The 18–39 group had a mean finishing time of approximately 212 minutes, while the 80+ group had a mean of approximately 301 minutes, a difference of 89 minutes. This gap is much larger than either group's standard error, suggesting a substantial difference between the estimated means. The standard deviations (45.4 and 30.1 minutes) show that individual finishing times vary considerably within each group, while the standard errors describe uncertainty in the estimated group means.

### B3 · Zoom or filter?

```{r}
#| label: fig-b3
#| ref.label: b3
#| echo: true

#| fig-subcap: ["Zoomed", "Filtered"]

#| layout: [[1, 1]]
```

```{r}
#| label: b3-check
#| include: false
```

WRITE (2–3 sentences): The zoomed plot makes differences between age-group counts appear much larger than they actually are. The filtered plot removes the smallest groups, making the remaining groups easier to compare but hiding information about the excluded groups. The Lie Factor of approximately 5 indicates that the zoomed visualization exaggerates apparent differences by about five times. I would prefer the plot starting at zero because it communicates the differences in group sizes more honestly.

WRITE (2 sentences): The 18–39 age group accounts for approximately 93% of everyone who finished in the top 100, while the 40–44 age group accounts for approximately 7%. This is different from B1 because B1 measures the rate within each age group, while B4 measures each group's contribution to the overall top-100 population.
